who-this-is-for.text: This page is for a holder of an active name who wants to change its payment destination, recover after losing the current controller, or retire permanently. Maintenance and recovery keep the representative in application custody. Retirement moves it into completion-only custody before burning it. The lifecycle contract is being integrated, so this page does not call an unavailable transition playable.

change-the-payment-destination.text: The controller may set, replace, or clear one optional payment destination. The destination is routing data, not authority. The sequence keeps the registry identity, key, representative, controller, next commitment, and quorum unchanged, and makes no registry request, mint, or burn. Wrong authority, multiple destinations, and control-field tampering are refused.

recover-with-the-committed-next-controll.text: Recovery reveals the complete next controller address, checks its canonical bytes against the domain-separated BLAKE two b two hundred and fifty six commitment, and requires its payment-key signer. The old controller need not sign. The successor keeps the representative, installs the revealed controller, and stores a fresh commitment. Only canonical base and enterprise payment-key addresses are supported.

retire-permanently.text: Either the controller or a sufficient reset quorum initiates retirement. Both routes put the representative into one completion-only request. Permissionless folding burns it and moves the key to Over. Pending retirement remains distinct from Over, and withdrawal, redirection, replay, Delete, release, and re-registration are refused.

what-remains-deliberately-unavailable.text: Cancelling an unfulfilled naming claim remains on hold. Insert certification never grants withdrawal permission, but the signer, refund recipient, refund value, and fee treatment are undecided. The naming interface therefore offers no withdrawal button or success claim. The generic registry demonstration is not naming policy.

consumer-and-ledger-boundary.text: The consumer contract is source-bound to a pinned cardano KERI commit. It uses Conway inline-datum and required-signer precedents without importing KERI schemas or claiming compiled-script interoperability. Singular publishes its own wire indices and field order, binds one registry identity per application, and rejects a rival initialization seed. The table separates what existing tooling constrains, what Singular publishes, and what remains outside the candidate.

evidence-and-release-status.text: The final browser surface must drive real integrated maintenance, recovery, and both retirement routes with their refusals. Placeholders are integration markers and cannot survive acceptance. The downloadable archive carries raw model, contract, scenarios, replay sources, pinned tooling, and exact identities under one SHA two hundred and fifty six manifest. This is still an unaccepted design candidate, not a deployed validator or ledger observation.
